The chapter's facts then ride on native furniture — the ride height post banded one to five is the staging system, the cast NO JUMPING notice with two lads over the rail is risk-taking as the venue's own hazard, the photo booth and the airbrush name stall are identity formation, and a knot of teenagers at the rail over families on the sand below is peers-versus-family as one bounded pair.

problems: Seafront crowding: chapter 42 (BEN'S DECKCHAIR HIRE — shingle beach below the promenade railing, hire hut, chalked rate board) and chapter 101 (O'CONNOR'S PRIZE DUCKS — "a promenade prize-shooting gallery ... between a rock shop and a chip shop") already occupy the seaside promenade. A pleasure pier makes three chapters in one register, and it additionally swallows the amusement arcade and the funfair as sub-premises.

Stock props restate chapter 42's almost item for item: "stack of folded windbreaks against the balustrade" (42 has the five-pole windbreak), "ice-cream kiosk price list" (42 has the ice-cream tricycle), "sun and tide board chalked up outside the kiosk" (42 has the chalked rate board on the hut step), turnstile counter dial and paper tickets (42 has the roll of punched hire tickets). R7 cue-distinctiveness fails on material and colour as well as object.

The venue stops being one place. It hosts four architectural-scale premises — an eight-ride luna park at the pier head, a five-lift scaffold tower mid-deck, a four-ward children's hospital on the front, and a slot saloon on the boards. That is chapter 3's declared job (MESSENGER ROW is the one chapter licensed to be a row of course-wide premises); duplicating it here means the chapter's retrieval hook is "the street with everything on it", which is already taken.

Density ceiling blown before the chapter's own content is drawn. Erikson alone is 8 rides x 2 poles with counted objects (~16-24 elements), Piaget is 4 wards, the ladder is 5 floors — roughly 30 sub-elements from tokens alone, against R6's 22-34 total. The chapter's five aspects (staging, identity, peers, risk, maturation) then have nowhere legible to sit.

hosts_tokens asserts a relation that is not drawn: the casino is called "the mesolimbic line's terminus" but no track, cart run or DOPA_MINE is in the frame — chapter 11 does not require it. A terminus with no line is an asserted fact, and R5 requires the link to be visible or dropped.

Minor: "TANNER'S PIER" is genuinely strong (eponym plus the PIER/PEER homophone, two chapter facts in two words) and the ride height post banded one to five, the cast NO JUMPING notice and the pier master's glass office are all excellent native carriers. The fascia should survive whatever replaces the pier.

The colliery gates close the top of the yard.

flagged.pun_explanation: Doubles, hards and duff are three genuine coal grades a merchant really paints on his board, and behind the proprietor's name their initials stand across the fascia as an ordered subsequence reading A-D-H-D — the expreSS tRIps device — while ADDERLEY is an ordinary English place-name carrying the stimulant in its first two syllables, and the diagnosis is never printed. The arcade was rejected because it shrank a course-wide fixed structure into a glass-cased penny model; moving the chapter to the foot of the pit road lets the colliery stand at full architectural scale at the head of the frame exactly as it does on Messenger Row. problems: The venue is coal, and coal is already spent twice. Chapter 4 (DOPA MINE No.4) is a working deep coal mine; chapter 3 (MESSENGER ROW) is closed at its head by "the colliery gates and winding gear ... with the four labelled underground sections opening off the gate yard". This proposal's DOPA_MINE clause is that sentence again — gates, winding gear, four labelled gallery mouths, carts running down the incline. Three chapters would open onto the same pit head.

R2 failure. The fixed token pops because it is an anomaly planted in a foreign world — a mine inside a kart track, inside a shop row. In a coal merchant's bagging yard the mine is the natural neighbour and stops being an anomaly at all; the whole frame is one material and one value key, so R7 and R8 lose their contrast as well.

NET token substituted, which the lexicon forbids. _lex.json binds NET to BEETHOVEN_ORCHESTRA (stage door of a concert hall, Beethoven in the white wig, numbered batons, heart-drums and winds sections). "The miners' institute band room ... the colliery band on the stand inside" is a different scene wearing the net. Policy is APPEND-ONLY: the venue changes, never the token.

DSM_neurodevelopmental is under-rendered and glazed off. The clause lists five corners' furniture (trains in a line, spilled kit, five-piece puzzle, floating letters, empty speech bubble) and never delivers the sixth (tic) corner, the six children themselves, or the teacher at the six-branch chart. It is also seen through school windows from across a lane — the same shrunk-behind-glass fault this rewrite claims to be fixing.

It rebuilds chapter 3's street: colliery at the head, board school across the lane, miners' institute across the lane, yard office over the weighbridge. Multi-premises containment is ch3's declared licence, not a repeatable device.
The fascia is five lettering units, at the spec's per-string cap, and the largest legible slot on the page goes to a four-word coal-grade list.
flagged.fix_hint: The acronym is the best thing in the batch — ADDERLEY'S / DOUBLES / HARDS / DUFF reading A-D-H-D as word-initials is exactly the expreSS tRIps device, and ADDER carries the stimulant besides. Keep it, and keep every criteria carrier (nine grades with six ticked, the two-round board, the date-stamped weigh-ticket spike, the minimum-load notice, the four chalked short-weight rejects) — those are native, digit-bearing and better than anything the arcade had. Change what the firm sells so the premises is not itself a coal business at the pit gate: the mine must arrive as a planted foreign neighbour the way it does on the kart track. Then restore Beethoven's stage door for NET and bring the six-corner classroom into the frame with its six children rather than its six empty corners.

flagged.activity: Everyone is matching boards — feeding a board into the moulder, taking it off at the outfeed, offering its tongue into the next board's groove on the assembly table, tapping it home with a scrap block, and standing the finished run up in a stick.
flagged.anchor_structure: The moulder and its long roller bed — the machine with its cutter heads and guards and the outfeed running away behind it — cutting the shop from the lower left of the frame to the upper right and dividing it into the infeed floor, the machine, the outfeed and assembly table, and the stacked runs by the loading door.
flagged.pun_explanation: Tongue-and-groove is a genuine joinery term and a name real joiners trade under, so the organ of articulation is lettered across the fascia of a trade with nothing whatever to do with speech, and the shop's ordinary business is literally getting one tongue to enter another's groove. The butcher was rejected as the third glass-counter, take-a-ticket, hanging-scale world after the deli and the wet fish shop, and this mill shares no furniture with any of them; the four subtypes then become shop-floor business rather than restated vignettes — boards with no tongue machined at all, or grooved on both edges so they can never join, are language disorder; boards run to the wrong profile so the joint stands proud are speech sound disorder; chatter, the mill's own word for a tool repeating the same cut, is stuttering on the machine's own vocabulary; and the posted feed rule with the man who keeps reaching into the outfeed out of turn is the social-pragmatic subtype. The setting-out mirror over the outfeed is already there for the therapist's move.

flagged.pun_explanation: RETT-A-DISH is the rent-a-X wrap said aloud, one eponym morpheme carried inside an utterly ordinary hire-trade fascia the same licence as TEAR-A-PLY ROOFING, and the diagnosis is never printed. The tool depot was rejected as the same trade-counter-and-racking room as the safety supplier, and the marquee yard offered in its place would have been a third tent-raising world after the circus and the flower show, so the pun moves to the hire trade that is a hand business rather than a counter one: wringing a cloth out and polishing every piece dry by hand is what this firm pays people to do all shift, so the hallmark hand movement is ordinary paid work and not a symbol of it. Retrieval runs backwards: a resident who remembers CLEAR SPRING FISHERIES recovers 'cerebrospinal fluid', and has to already be thinking about lumbar puncture to get from there to meningitis. Rule 1 asks the name to be a pun on the topic; this is a pun on the test.

C-S-F as three word-initials is the weakest legal form of ACRONYM_EMBED. The corpus precedents work for reasons this one lacks: OUSE AMATEUR ROWING SOCIETY spells OARS, which is both a real word and the method's own four-skill acronym; OCEAN DAILY CATCH and expreSS tRIps bury the letters inside words. The trade then pays out on the rest as ordinary site business rather than as metaphor. A fishery numbers its pegs, so loci get carriers whose real job is to bear digits: peg 22 on the near staging, peg 7 where the aerator pipework runs, peg 15 on both banks. The two waters are named on one post at the path fork, ANGEL POOL and WILLOW POOL, so the two syndromes ride on ordinary lake names; and because the same peg 15 exists on both waters and the day ticket is stamped with which one you are on, the venue's own geography is genomic imprinting — one deleted stretch, and which side it came from decides everything about the day. Prader-Willi is the fishery's own posted food law: the bait limit chalked on the rules board and the bait freezer standing padlocked and chained outside the hut, which is food security drawn with nothing invented. Hypocalcaemia is the split bag of lime and the water-hardness test card by the hatch, both genuine fishery kit; the thymus is the pair of small bait tins gone from the shelf with their rings left in the dust; the cleft is the split down the middle of the landing-net mesh; and the heart is the restart cabinet screwed to the hut wall. Williams is peg 7: the section of aerator hose pinched tight just above its stopcock, and the transistor radio going at the one peg where the angler is talking to everybody. The match draw bag of numbered wooden discs on the hut counter is the whole business of which peg you get, drawn blind.

flagged.place: The night shift in the No. 4 spinning room of a cotton mill: one ring frame running the whole length of the room with its rows of spindles whirring, the creel of roving bobbins above it, the lineshaft and its belts under the ceiling, gas mantles down the alley, and the end window looking out over the mill gate.
flagged.activity: Everyone is minding the frames — walking the alley watching for a broken end, piecing the ends up between finger and thumb, sweeping the fly off the rails, and lifting the full cops off the spindles into a skip when the doffing call goes round.
flagged.anchor_structure: The ring frame — one continuous machine the length of the room, its ring rail rising and falling along a row of spindles, the roving creel above it and the lineshaft and belts overhead — running from the lower left of the frame to the upper right and dividing the room into the doffing alley, the frame itself, the creel and gearing end, and the stair-and-hoist bay by the window.
flagged.pun_explanation: A mill's whole capacity is counted in spindles, so the fascia is an ordinary mill name and the second stage's named waveform at the same time, and the word sleep is nowhere on the board. The isomorphism is the machine's own motion rather than a metaphor laid over it: the ring rail rises and falls all night long and lays the cop down in visible layers, four or five builds to a doff, with the deepest part of the traverse coming early in the build and the run at the top of it getting longer towards the end — a night's architecture drawn as ordinary machinery a resident can redraw from memory. The frame whose driving belt has been thrown off its pulley while every spindle on it still whirrs at full speed is the paradoxical stage, drive cut to everything that moves and nothing else slowed at all. The overlooker's round comes every ninety minutes, which is the cycle at its real length. The light-and-clock system that the circadian disorders break is all standing furniture here: the mill clock over the door, the timekeeper's board with the shift hours painted on, the gas mantle turned right down over the far end of the alley, and the knocker-up's pole and cap hung inside the door with its list of streets and times. The humidifier duct in the ceiling with its damper half shut and two swollen bags of fly jammed in the throat of it is the obstructed airway and its adenotonsillar cause on one object; the shaft bearing that rattles, falls silent, and then bangs is the snore with the pause in the middle of it. The doffer who cannot stand still and shakes one leg out against the frame leg between skips is restless legs, and the ages down the alley, from the half-timer at the creel to the old sweeper at the far end, carry the lifespan without a word being written.
